SYMPTOMS: Yellow leaf tips, brown spots
Tap-water salts plus low light — what your small broad-leaf plant is showing
Flush the pot through with plenty of water once, move it closer to the glass, stop wetting the leaves.
Lower leaves yellow, soil still damp
Overwatering, worst July–September in a closed room
Stop watering. Open a window. If the stem is soft at soil level, cut above the rot and re-root the top.
Everything leaning at the window
Directional light, unavoidable in a room
Rotate every pot a quarter turn weekly. Free, and it is the whole fix.
Succulent stretching and pale
Not enough light — expected until the grow light arrives
Move to the glass or switch the lamp on. Behead and re-root the stretched top to restart it compact.
Grey film, growth slowing
Coal and fly-ash dust
Wipe weekly with a damp cloth, rinse monthly.
Crispy brown leaf edges
Dry inland air, worst March–May near 50% humidity
Group plants, pebble trays, mist the back-of-room ones daily.
Whole plant dies back in December
Normal dormancy if your tall ones are turmeric
Do not throw the pot out. Keep it barely damp; it re-sprouts from the rhizome in spring.
Sudden collapse after a cold night
Chill damage below 10°C, December–January
Move tropicals away from the glass at night — it radiates heat away fast. Do not cut damage until March.
Whole shelf wilting on a hot afternoon
Trapped heat in a closed glazed room
Open windows, run the fan. Check the room at 3pm in April before it becomes a May crisis.
White cottony blobs in leaf joints
Mealybug — arrives on nearly every online order
Cotton bud with rubbing alcohol, then neem weekly for three weeks, done outside the room.
Fine webbing, speckled leaves
Spider mites — they love hot dry March to May
Rinse leaves hard, then neem. Raising humidity genuinely helps.
Tiny black flies at the pot
Fungus gnats in wet cocopeat
Let the top 2 cm dry fully. Yellow sticky traps. Safe around mushrooms.
Jade leaves shrivelling and dropping
Either too little water, or rot from neat Magic Soil
Check the stem base. Firm means water it. Soft means unpot, cut back to clean tissue, repot gritty.
ROOMS: Front row, against the open grille
Mesh slid aside, nothing between plant and sky. Your only real light.
Still bright, no direct beam. Compact succulents, orchids, bonsai.
Light falls off fast in a room. Ferns, aroids, pitchers.
Screen glow and a little window light — and the cleanest air in the house.
